source: Written for Wayword as a learner's guide; not part of the original dataset. Examples are dataset phrases.
intro: Italian is pronounced almost exactly as it's written. The two things to train are double consonants and the c/g rules.
reading: CAPITALS mark the stress, usually on the second-to-last syllable.
Every vowel is said, including the last one: per favore ends in a clear "eh".
Doubled letters in the pronunciation (kahf-FEH, vor-RAY) mean hold the consonant.

sounds.name: Double consonants
sounds.how: Hold a doubled consonant for longer, with a tiny pause before releasing it. The difference changes meaning (pala/palla, caro/carro).

sounds.name: Soft C and G
sounds.how: Before i or e, c = ch and g = j. The i is often just a spelling signal: ciao is "chow", giorno is "JOR-noh".

sounds.name: Hard C and G
sounds.how: Adding an h keeps them hard: chi is "kee", che is "keh".

sounds.name: GN and GLI
sounds.how: gn = ny as in "canyon" (bagno is "BAH-nyoh"). gli = a soft ly, like the lli in "million".

sounds.name: SC
sounds.how: Before i or e, sc = sh (lascia is "LAH-shah"). Before other vowels it's sk (capisco).

sounds.name: Z
sounds.how: z is ts (grazie is "GRAH-tsyeh"), or dz in some words. It's never the English z.

sounds.name: Rolled R
sounds.how: A tap, or a short trill, with the tip of the tongue. A double rr is a full trill.

tips_source: "How it's said" tips are written for Wayword (not part of the dataset): how a speaker of standard Italian says the phrase at normal speed, next to the careful pronunciation line.

tips.dont_speak_well: The n of non turns into m before the p of parlo: nom PAR-loh BEH-neh ee-tah-LYAH-noh.
tips.dont_understand: The n of non sounds like ng before the k sound: nong kah-PEE-skoh.
tips.say_again: In standard Italian, può doubles the r after it: pwor-ree-PEH-teh-reh. Stress the second syllable of ripetere, not the third.
tips.speak_slowly: In standard Italian, stressed words like può and più double the consonant after them: pwop-par-LAH-reh pyool-len-tah-MEN-teh.
tips.how_say: In standard Italian, come doubles the s of si: KOH-mehs-see DEE-cheh.
tips.learning_by_trying: In standard Italian, a doubles the p of parlare: ap-par-LAH-reh. Imparo is stressed on PAH, not on the last syllable.
tips.is_far: In standard Italian, è doubles the l that follows: el-lon-TAH-noh. Many northern speakers don't double it.
tips.coffee: The n of un sounds like ng before the k sound of caffè: oong kahf-FEH.
tips.whats_in_this: In standard Italian, c'è doubles the d of dentro: KOH-zah chehd-DEN-troh.
tips.people_tip: In standard Italian, qui doubles the s of si: kwees-see LAH-shah lah MAHN-chah.
tips.your_name: In standard Italian, come doubles the t of ti: KOH-meht-tee KYAH-mee.
tips.where_from: In standard Italian, dove doubles the s of sei: dee DOH-vehs-SAY.
tips.what_do_you_do: In standard Italian, che doubles the l of lavoro: kel-lah-VOH-roh fai.
tips.me_too: Anch'io is one word with the stress on io, and the n sounds like ng before the k: ahng-KEE-oh.
tips.and_you: In standard Italian, e doubles the t of tu: et-TOO.
